## 13/09/2026 18:51 — VoiceBridge Market + Enterprise V002

Partner, I went beyond the V001 defect review and assessed **whether this is actually worth building as a market product**.

### My conclusion

**Yes, there is real market demand — but I would NOT sell VoiceBridge simply as another “Salesforce CTI”.**

The category is already validated and commercially active: Salesforce AppExchange has established products from Five9, Talkdesk, Vonage, NICE, Dialpad and others. citeturn0search3turn0search4turn0search9 Salesforce's own research also shows strong investment in service technology and rapidly increasing AI adoption. citeturn0search0turn0search5

So I scored it:

| Assessment | Score |
|---|---:|
| **Market demand** | **7/10 — YES** |
| Current enterprise readiness | **3/10 — NO** |
| Current differentiation | **4/10 — WEAK** |
| Worth continuing to build | **9/10 — YES, if repositioned** |

The key is the positioning. I recommend moving from **“Salesforce CTI / softphone”** toward a **“Salesforce Conversation Productivity & Revenue Workflow Layer”**: real voice + automatic CRM capture + AI after-call work + next actions + Flow automation + analytics + BYOT/provider neutrality.

That gives VoiceBridge a better reason to exist instead of trying to out-Five9 Five9 or out-Talkdesk Talkdesk.

### I created the full Claude build roadmap

The V002 workbook contains **19 enhancement sprints and 148 new build stories**, taking it from the present prototype toward enterprise grade.

The roadmap deliberately starts with **market validation**, then real telephony/Salesforce integration, OAuth/identity, Postgres multi-tenancy, enterprise RBAC, observability/SRE, security/compliance, Salesforce packaging, real WhatsApp, AI assist, revenue intelligence, APIs, privacy/residency, scale certification, supportability, **paid design-partner pilots**, commercial economics, independent AppExchange review and finally GA.

I also carried forward **all 14 V001 findings**, so Claude cannot accidentally lose the existing 5 BLOCKER + 5 HIGH + 4 MEDIUM findings while adding new features.

Most importantly, the workbook contains a **Claude Build Protocol**: no mock-only closure, every defect requires a permanent regression, exact release hashes/evidence, live Postgres/provider/Salesforce evidence where required, tenant-boundary tests, no false “Done” status, and **STOP after failed P0 gates rather than continuing to pile code on top**.

**Download the V002 Excel:**

This is the file I would give Claude as the **next build master**, rather than asking Claude simply to continue the existing 96/100 backlog.

## 13/09/2026 17:34 — VoiceBridge Salesforce Review

Partner, completed the **independent product + code + documentation + workbook review** across the latest **v0.23.0 codebase / product workbook v023 / tracker v017**, with the earlier versions used for comparison.

**Decision: 🔴 REJECT — not yet pilot-ready, production-ready, or AppExchange-ready.**

The review found **14 findings: 5 BLOCKER, 5 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM**. The biggest issues are not cosmetic: the Salesforce OAuth callback flow is incompatible, the softphone does not send the new bearer session, installer identity is still caller-declared, Postgres is not wired into the running application, and the supposed CTI path does **not actually place a telephony call or write the activity back to Salesforce**.

I also found that the supplied security/test evidence is stale—it is dated **11 Sep**, reports **24 suites / 101 tests**, and even references the now-deleted `store.ts`, so it cannot serve as release evidence for the 13 Sep v0.23.0 package.

The review document includes exact code evidence, impact, required correction, and **permanent regression test for every finding**, plus workbook/traceability assessment, financial-model review, v0.22→v0.23 delta, closure order, and final acceptance gate.
